title: Creotech Quantum Wins €2.33M ($2.66M USD) ESA Contract for Space-Grade Quantum Detectors - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Warsaw-listed Creotech Quantum (GPW: CTQ) will lead ESA's €2.33M, 24-month HRQKD consortium, taking €1.2M as prime contractor to take superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs) from prototype to TRL 5 for optical ground stations serving EuroQCI, IRIS² and deep-space optical links. It is a short news brief (~370 words), so the signal is mainly the deal terms and where Creotech sits in Europe's sovereign quantum-communications supply chain.

insights.claim: Creotech Quantum S.A. (GPW: CTQ) signed a €2.33 million ($2.66M) European Space Agency contract, called HRQKD (High-Rate Quantum Key Distribution), to lead an international consortium developing next-generation single-photon detectors.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Winning a prime ESA contract gives a small-cap Warsaw quantum stock credibility, but the deal is small next to its funding needs, so it confirms the story more than it moves revenue.
insights.locator: Warsaw-listed quantum infrastructure vendor Creotech Quantum

insights.claim: Of ESA's €2.33M HRQKD budget, €1.2 million ($1.37M), about 52%, goes directly to Creotech Quantum as prime contractor. The remaining ~€1.13M is spread across the other consortium partners.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: €1.2M over 24 months is roughly €0.6M a year of revenue to CTQ. Size any revenue model on that figure, not the €2.33M headline.
insights.quote: allocates €1.2 million ($1.37 million USD) directly to Creotech Quantum as prime contractor
insights.locator: Warsaw-listed quantum infrastructure vendor Creotech Quantum

insights.claim: The ESA HRQKD project runs on a 24-month schedule and aims to take SNSPD detection hardware from proof-of-concept prototypes to Technology Readiness Level 5 (TRL 5), validated in simulated industrial and space-ground environments.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: TRL 5 is still pre-product, and flight or operational deployment (TRL 7-9) would need follow-on contracts. Watch around 2028 for a follow-on qualification or production award.
insights.quote: from proof-of-concept prototypes to Technology Readiness Level 5 (TRL 5)

insights.claim: Creotech Quantum's HRQKD deliverables include the Superconducting Nanowire Single-Photon Detectors (SNSPDs) plus integrated readout electronics and control software. Creotech is responsible for design, manufacture and validation.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Creotech is being paid for a full detector subsystem, not just a component, which could move it up the value chain toward complete ground-station receivers.
insights.locator: [ ESA HRQKD Project Architecture & Financial Scope ]

insights.claim: The SNSPDs are core components of optical ground stations that receive space-to-ground quantum signals across European satellite programmes, including EuroQCI, IRIS², ARTES, SAGA and ScyLight.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Detector suppliers are the 'picks and shovels' of EU sovereign quantum-secure communications. Budget decisions for EuroQCI and IRIS² drive demand for ground-station hardware.

insights.claim: Ultra-low-noise SNSPD systems can also serve high-bandwidth deep-space optical communication, where received signals are extremely faint, such as lunar base links and deep-space science probes. That makes the market bigger than QKD key reception alone.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Being able to sell into both QKD and deep-space optical comms lowers the risk that QKD adoption is slow. Lunar and deep-space laser comms programmes are a second source of demand.
insights.quote: enable high-bandwidth deep-space optical communication where received signals are extremely faint, such as lunar base links and deep-space science probes

insights.claim: The HRQKD project's stated deployment scope covers satellite-to-ground QKD networks (EuroQCI, IRIS²), deep-space optical laser communications, and defense, telecom and critical-infrastructure links.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The defense and critical-infrastructure angle ties the technology to rising European security budgets. Treat that as optional upside, since no customers are named.
insights.locator: [ ESA HRQKD Project Architecture & Financial Scope ]

insights.claim: Creotech Quantum, led by CEO Dr. Anna Kamińska, heads the HRQKD consortium and oversees electronics engineering, software architecture, environmental testing and product roadmap development.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Owning the product roadmap as consortium lead suggests Creotech means to turn the SNSPD work into its own product line rather than just deliver a one-off R&D project.
insights.locator: Led by CEO Dr. Anna Kamińska

insights.claim: Creotech Quantum was spun out of satellite manufacturer Creotech Instruments. It builds on in-house electronics production, White Rabbit sub-nanosecond time synchronization and Sinara/MTCA control systems to supply European quantum hardware supply chains.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Space heritage from its parent plus control-electronics know-how (Sinara, White Rabbit) gives Creotech a real edge as an EU-sovereign quantum enabling-tech supplier. Worth tracking alongside Creotech Instruments.
insights.locator: Spun out from satellite manufacturer Creotech Instruments

insights.claim: Creotech Quantum describes itself as a 'quantum infrastructure vendor' (enabling hardware, electronics and synchronization) rather than a quantum-computer builder. That puts it among the suppliers who can sell to every quantum platform, whichever one wins.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Enabling-tech vendors earn revenue earlier and carry less technology risk than qubit-modality bets. Value CTQ as a hardware and components supplier, not a quantum-compute option.
insights.quote: Warsaw-listed quantum infrastructure vendor Creotech Quantum S.A. (GPW: CTQ)
insights.locator: Warsaw-listed quantum infrastructure vendor Creotech Quantum
